definitions.explanation: A retail shop or store, typically a smaller independent establishment. Often used in compound forms, especially in {商店街|しょうてんがい} (shopping street/district).

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{小|ちい}さな→小さな：02913_chiisana⟧{商店|しょうてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a small shop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いて→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I walked through the shopping street and did some shopping.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地方|ちほう}→地方：02369_chihou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦シャッター{通|どお}り→シャッター通り：29816_shattaadoori⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれる→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧ほど⟦{閉店|へいてん}→閉店：09698_heiten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{相次|あいつ}いでいる→相次ぐ：14869_aitsugu⟧。
examples.english: Shopping streets in rural areas have seen so many closures that they are called 'shutter streets.'

notes:
Most commonly encountered in the compound ⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧ (shopping street, shopping district) — a traditional row of small shops along a street, often covered with an arcade. These are a distinctive feature of Japanese neighborhoods.

As standalone {商店|しょうてん}, it sounds somewhat formal. In everyday speech, ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧ or ⟦お{店|みせ}→お店：21164_omise⟧ is more common for 'shop.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧ — shopping street, shopping district
- {商店|しょうてん}{主|しゅ} — shopkeeper
- ⟦{個人|こじん}→個人：02758_kojin⟧{商店|しょうてん} — independently owned shop
- {商店|しょうてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧ — shops line up (along a street)
